sections.title: 3c. Subagent dispatch discipline
sections.summary: Background dispatch never blocks the main session; the model and thinking level come from `.env.local`, are used as dispatch parameters only, and are never printed or committed.

rules.text: After dispatching you must register the executor (a **self-declared ledger**, not identity proof): `config.set executor.<rN>.<stage>=<agent_id>`, stage ∈ analysis / plan / development; when one subagent covers all three stages, register the same id stage by stage. Replacing the executor for the same (req, stage) with a different id **requires** a reason (`=<new_id>|<reason>`); a **cross-stage handoff** (a plan id different from the analysis one, or — with no plan — different from the analysis one) equally requires a reason and may never be silently overwritten as a "first binding for that stage". A successful handoff writes `id|reason` and appends one entry to `req.<i>.hist` (reusing the rolling cap; no separate history/handoff key); a clean first binding writes no history. The ledger carries no rev: `amend` does not change the binding and `split` / `merge` do not inherit it. `proposal.submit` performs no hard check — an unregistered executor only shows as "unregistered" in `requirement.list` and never blocks external proposals or same-ext replays.
rules.basis: user decision 2026-11-01 (E2 ruling: reuse config.set, bind no rev, no hard submit gate, a cross-stage handoff must give a reason)

rules.text: A genuinely new architectural decision gets its `D-MAx` number allocated serially by the main session at dispatch time and written into the requirement description and the subagent brief; an existing decision reuses its existing number. An executor never self-allocates `max+1`: two lanes picking `max+1` from the same base double-claimed `D-MA16` (see docs/CONTEXT.md history `d0b4a7c` / `6848138`). IDs beyond the brief are not self-served — return to the coordinator.

Every subagent task runs in the background; the main session never waits in place — keep advancing other lanes, verifications or planning while it runs, and verify and merge once the completion notice arrives.
Synchronous waiting is allowed only when the next action strictly depends on the result and nothing else can progress in parallel; even then, spend the waiting time on other lanes first.

Before dispatching, read the repository-root `.env.local` (git-ignored, never committed): `YGG_SUBAGENT_MODEL` (the subagent model, e.g. `sonnet` / `provider/model-id`) and `YGG_SUBAGENT_THINKING` (`off|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max`); when unset, pass nothing explicitly and use the harness default.
These two values are dispatch parameters only — never printed, never written into documentation, never committed.

sections.title: 4. Develop → integrate → merge → deploy
sections.summary: Three closing levels: the iteration point (feature → develop) → the round (develop → master, user-triggered) → deployment; integration, merging and deployment are always done serially by the main agent.

rules.text: Integration, merging and deployment are executed serially by the main agent (the main session); lane subagents only develop, pass their gates and push their feature branch — a subagent never merges into `develop`, never pushes `develop`, and never rebases another lane's branch.
First step of an iteration closeout: `git fetch origin`.

All gates must be green on the feature branch itself before integration starts (see the gates chapter) — this admission check is purely branch-local evidence, and it never carries over: after the feature lands in `develop` the integrated state is tested again (`integration.iter.test-after-integrate`).

Before rebasing, check that local `develop` and `origin/develop` have not diverged: if they have diverged, stop, analyse and report to the user instead of resolving it automatically; otherwise `git pull origin develop --ff-only`.
rules.basis: user decision (r2): develop-normalized git integration workflow

rules.text: Rebase the feature branch onto the local `develop` — this is the standing path for every requirement closeout, not an exception.
rules.basis: user decision (r2): develop-normalized git integration workflow

rules.text: When the rebase conflicts, stop the whole-branch rebase and replay commit by commit with `git cherry-pick`; land each conflict as its own standalone conflict-resolution commit so every step stays auditable.
rules.basis: user decision (r2): develop-normalized git integration workflow

rules.text: After any history rewrite (rebase or cherry-pick replay), push with `git push --force-with-lease origin <feature>`; a bare push is forbidden.
rules.basis: user decision (r2): develop-normalized git integration workflow

rules.text: In the main checkout, merge the feature branch into `develop` using the local ref — `git merge --no-ff <feature>` — then push `develop`; deleting the remote feature branch stays optional.
rules.basis: user decision (r2): develop-normalized git integration workflow

rules.text: Never merge `origin/feature/*`: after a rebase the remote ref still points at the old head, so merging it fabricates duplicate same-content commits plus an orphaned merge node — merge only the local ref.
rules.basis: user decision (r2): develop-normalized git integration workflow

rules.text: After a feature lands in `develop`, re-run the gates and E2E on the integrated state in the main checkout; the feature-branch admission green never carries over — an iteration point closes on integrated-state evidence.
rules.basis: user decision (r2): develop-normalized git integration workflow

rules.text: Pushing the feature branch alone is not a closeout: a requirement closes only after it is merged into `develop` and tested on the integrated state — `develop` must never lag behind completed features.
rules.basis: user decision (r2): develop-normalized git integration workflow

rules.text: A round-level closeout first passes end-to-end acceptance on the `develop` integrated state once every in-round feature has landed: the example game completed end to end plus save/load verification; after M1 this adds the AI-generated → playable loop — the precondition for merging into `master`.
Integration and the `master` merge are two separate stages and never execute as one: while any in-round feature has not landed in `develop` yet, merging into `master` is forbidden.
rules.basis: user decision (r2): develop-normalized git integration workflow

rules.text: The `develop` → `master` merge is triggered by the user, or executed by the main agent after the user approves it: `git fetch origin`, then divergence-check `master` and `develop` separately and align each with `--ff-only`, then in the main checkout `git merge --no-ff develop`, then `git push origin master` — the merge is not complete until the trunk is pushed; rebasing `develop` is absolutely forbidden — the merge topology is the rollback history.
rules.basis: user decision (r2): develop-normalized git integration workflow

rules.text: Right after the merge, `git reset --hard master` on `develop` so `develop` equals `master` as the clean baseline for the next round; push both branches — for `develop` the reset makes it `git push --force-with-lease origin develop`.
rules.basis: user decision (r2): develop-normalized git integration workflow

rules.text: Once acceptance passes, tag the batch `v<YYYY.MM.DD>.<n>` — the no-FF merge node is the rollback anchor.
A batch closeout updates the CHANGELOG / report when one exists.
Anything deployed through any channel must already be merged into master: a non-master ref is refused outright, with no exception switch.
Deployment is a write operation: report it to the user and get approval before every deployment.

sections.title: 5. Verification-command gates
sections.summary: The gate baseline is a snapshot: the acceptance standard is "introduce no new failure"; a module whose gate is not wired up must be declared uncovered explicitly.

rules.text: The gate baseline is a snapshot that grows with each iteration, and the acceptance standard is "introduce no new failure" — historical debt does not have to be zero, but no new failure may appear.

The three-suite green of this repository is claimed only by running the three commands verbatim (`cargo test --workspace`; `cargo test --example egg -p ygg-sandbox`; `cargo test -p ygg-sandbox --test agent_seed_semantics`) and recording each command with its real exit code and test counts. Member-equivalent runs (`cargo check`, single-test selections, filtered runs), `verify-suite --mode fast`, and any `YGG_VERIFY_COMMANDS` override are evidence of the substitute only and never substitute for the literal suite evidence.
rules.basis: user decision 2026-11-12 (E7: member-equivalent runs masked kernel_facade runtime failures in two consecutive runs)

rules.text: The dependency list in `ygg-core`'s `Cargo.toml` is part of the review: a rendering, platform or IO dependency is a violation with no exception mechanism.
A module whose gate is not wired up yet (no tests exist) must be declared "gate not covered" in the report; it never passes by default.

Changing `.ygg/mods/agent-seed/src/**` (state machine / gates / render layer), `mod.lua`, or the map wording in `.ygg/mods/agent-seed/data/scenes.json` adds `cargo test -p ygg-sandbox --test agent_seed_semantics` to the gate list on top of lint and the all-1 playtest: the case list = stage merge plus the compatibility `analysis` slot / accept-gate reject / accept-gate approval releasing the lane / accept-gate amend → stale / plan-gate reject / reactive auto-dispatch in the same turn (with `useMemo` invalidation) / development proposal reject (not amended and amended) / inline `exec=` (misplaced, missing reason, `:` form) / settlement merge with `sessions=` + `todo=` and a refused malformed segment / legacy save without `plan_ok` / the operation-map wording (payload-independent single view) plus the guide.show deregistration (empty narrative, no menu entry) on both packs / the all-1 walk of both packs / the six active-subsystem cases (`worktree_claim` + release, lane probe + conflict radar blocking `coordinate.submit`, artifact probe + `vfs.write` ledger, `gate.verify_suite` green evidence, `harness.archive_sessions` settlement, declaration completeness). The all-1 playtest only covers the happy path — it never takes a branch (`gate.reject` / `requirement.amend` / `proposal.reject`) and cannot see the turn-cut mechanics at all; a temporary probe under `/tmp` may only supplement this test and never replace it; every uncovered scenario must be declared item by item in the report. Three-question criterion: ① the blocked action is "change the Mod source or the map wording, run only lint plus all-1, and call it accepted"; ② the visible symptom of a violation is that branch semantics and map wording regress while every gate stays green, so the defect only shows in a real run; ③ confirm it next time with that command (29/29) plus one mutation probe (put the old semantics back → the test must go red) to prove the assertions are not vacuous.

Never build the wasm bindings with wasm-pack: the exception-handling module needs `wasm-bindgen --reference-types` and wasm-pack does not pass that flag through; the build chain is fixed to `scripts/build-wasm.sh` (cargo plus the wasm-bindgen CLI, two steps).

When the FR-9 dual-run state hashes differ, never silently edit the fixture baseline — a mismatch is a determinism breach between platforms, and a baseline change requires an explicit decision plus a record.

Before claiming full FR-9 compliance, add the wasm-bindgen-test browser lane (replay the same assertions in a real browser wasm instance) or take an explicit waiver decision; today the node lane covers native/wasm dual-run equivalence, and the browser lane does not exist.

Contract parity criterion: the same Mod sample must produce identical results through ajv and through the jsonschema crate; the CI script does not exist yet, so until it lands that surface is declared "gate not covered".
